absent: Exact numeric values and ordering of zone types, migrate types, section and pageblock sizes, and online policy constants.
Lifecycle and reset conditions for first_deferred_pfn and deferred page initialization after boot.
Semantics of move_pfn_range_to_zone, remove_pfn_range_from_zone, online_pages_range, undo_isolate_page_range, shuffle_zone, setup_zone_pageset, and init_per_zone_wmark_min.
Notifier chain effects, veto behavior, and consumer obligations for memory and node online stages.
Memory group creation, static versus dynamic membership rules, and unit size selection.
Zonelist reader locking and iteration protocol beyond the writer side shown.
Writeback dirty-limit computation and ratelimit consumption path.

findings.text: Initialization entry for a zone that is currently empty. It widens the node zone count when the index requires it, records the start frame number, emits a memmap init trace, prepares buddy free lists, and marks the zone initialized.

Public entry to online a frame range into a zone and memory group. It validates the range, associates frames with the zone, drives node and memory notifications, updates population and zonelists, releases isolation, shuffles the zone, refreshes watermarks and background threads, and rolls the association back on failure.

Zone selection dispatcher for a frame range. It honors an explicit kernel or movable request, otherwise follows the configured online policy by choosing automatic movable evaluation or default inheritance.

Counter maintenance entry when frames are added or removed. It resolves the owning zone from the page, updates zone and node present counts including early counts, and attributes the delta to the movable or kernel tally of the supplied group.

Zonelist rebuild entry. It takes a boot-time path during early boot and a runtime path otherwise, then recomputes free pages beyond high watermark, toggles mobility grouping based on system size, and reports the result.

Boot-time zonelist initialization entry. It builds all zonelists, initializes per-CPU boot pagesets and zone statistics for bootstrapping, then verifies zonelists and initializes current memory allowance.
Query entry returning the local memory node for a given node by inspecting the first usable entry of the node's fallback list at the normal allocation zone level.
Section state entry that marks every memory section in a frame interval offline by clearing its online flag, stepping one section at a time.
Writeback tuning entry that recomputes global dirty limits, stores the dirty limit in the global domain, and derives a per-CPU ratelimit with a minimum floor.

Self-hosted map initialization entry for hot-added ranges. It establishes shadow state, moves the range into the target zone as unmovable, clears offline state and marks pages self-hosted, and marks fully covered sections online.
Self-hosted map teardown entry. It marks fully covered sections offline, removes the frame range from its zone, and releases the associated shadow state.

Deferred page initialization policy has two builds. One build never defers. The other refuses deferral when page extensions are active, when the range ends below the node end so constrained zones stay populated, and otherwise starts deferring only after about one section of early pages, recording the first deferred frame on a section boundary and treating later calls as deferred.
Zone free-list preparation initializes every free list head, zeroes the free count for every order, and additionally initializes the unaccepted pages list when that feature is enabled.

Early init diagnostics have two builds: a conditional logging form that compares a level against a global log level and routes warnings versus debug output with a fixed prefix, and a no-operation inline form that accepts the same arguments and does nothing.
Node or zone level movable census holds two counters: early kernel pages and movable pages. Group level census holds movable pages and required early kernel pages used for ratio accounting.

Zone accounting treats the movable zone as fully movable and other zones as early kernel, with an adjustment that moves contiguous reservation pages from the early kernel tally to the movable tally. Group accounting derives required early kernel pages from present movable pages and a configured percentage ratio, ignoring nonpositive demand.

Movable admission collects kernel versus movable totals either globally or for one node, subtracts the demand attributed to other dynamic groups, credits kernel pages of the current dynamic group, adds the candidate pages to movable, and admits only when the percentage ratio constraint still holds.
Default kernel zone selection scans zones below the normal zone in order and returns the first one intersecting the candidate range, falling back to the normal zone when none intersects.

Automatic movable placement refuses movable when the ratio is disabled, forces kernel placement when a static group already holds kernel pages or when any examined online section in a dynamic unit is non-movable, aligns dynamic evaluation to unit boundaries, requires both global and optionally node-local ratio admission for all remaining unit pages, and otherwise selects the movable zone.

Default zone inheritance returns the uniquely intersecting zone when exactly one of the kernel or movable zones intersects the range; when neither or both intersect it follows a movable-node enablement flag, defaulting to the kernel zone.

Onlining requires a nonempty pageblock aligned range whose end is section aligned. It pre-accounts isolation blocks, initializes the zone pageset and rebuilds zonelists when the zone becomes newly populated, updates present counts after mapping the range online, sets node memory states, then unisolates, shuffles, refreshes watermarks, starts reclaim and compaction threads, and announces completion.

Online lifecycle notifications progress from going-online to online on success, or to cancel-online on failure. First memory on a node additionally progresses from adding-first-memory to added-first-memory on success, or to cancel-adding-first-memory on failure, with rollback removing the range from the zone.

Onlining mutates the isolated-block counter under the zone lock with interrupts saved. Zonelist rebuilds hold the zonelist update sequence lock for writing with interrupts saved because readers may run in interrupt context, and enter deferred printing around the rebuild to avoid printk lock interaction.
Deferred-init bookkeeping uses file-local static state without locking on the grounds that it runs very early before secondary CPU initialization, resetting its counter when the zone end changes.

Zonelist construction appends per-node zone references in node order and terminates each list with a null zone entry. Per-node construction walks zone types from high to low, includes only populated zones, and records the highest populated type. One build orders nodes by NUMA distance with a round-robin load adjustment and builds both fallback and node-local lists; the other build creates a single-node fallback list.

Free-page census for mobility grouping sums, over the current node fallback list from a zone offset, the excess of managed pages above the high watermark. Mobility grouping is disabled when that total is below one pageblock per migrate type and enabled otherwise.

Ratio handling must avoid division by zero when the configured automatic movable ratio is zero. Online range validation warns once on empty or misaligned ranges. Hot-added node rebuild must handle a node with no online memory by building only that node.
Zone roles distinguish a movable zone from kernel zones ordered below and including the normal zone, with a maximum zone count bounding iteration.
Online control vocabulary includes explicit kernel and movable online types and an automatic movable policy selector that enables ratio based placement.

Hotplug lifecycle vocabulary includes going-online, online and cancel-online memory stages, adding-first-memory, added-first-memory and cancel variants for nodes, and node memory versus normal-memory states.
